newsitem.title: ZAIRE: UN delays Rwanda repatriation over cholera fears.
newsitem.headline: UN delays Rwanda repatriation over cholera fears.

text.p: The U.N. refugee agency has decided to delay the start of an operation to repatriate tens of thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees from Zaire because of fears that cholera is spreading in the area.
The governor of Upper Zaire region had expressed concern that the programme could jeapordise the health of local residents, UNHCR regional spokesman Paul Stromberg said on Thursday.
"The governor invoked health concerns worrying that the operation might somehow propogate cholera," Stromberg told reporters in the Zairean town of Kisingani.
"We are optimistic that they (regional authorities) will conclude that this is safe to do and that we will be able to start on Saturday," Stromberg said.
A total of 330 cholera cases and 19 cholera deaths have been recorded at Kasese refugee camp, 25 km (miles) south of Kisangani, according to U.N. figures.
Around 100,000 sick and exhausted Rwandan refugees arrived near a railway line south of Zaire's third city Kisangani last month begging to go home after a five-month trek through the jungle.
Newly elected governor Yagi Sitolo told Reuters he feared cholera could spread if refugees were brought to Kisangani airport for the flight home.
Senior aid officials planned to meet regional authorities on Friday in an effort to convince them the repatriation posed no threat, Stromberg said.

U.N. agencies and non-governmental organisations are nursing the refugees back to health and UNHCR has devised a multi-million dollar plan to take the refugees on trucks, planes and barges across the Zaire river back to Rwanda.
Eighty healthy but unaccompanied Rwandan children were to be flown to the eastern town of Goma on Friday at the start of the opeation.

Rebels of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo/Zaire control more than half of Zaire after a six-month campaign to oust ailing president Mobutu Sese Seko, Zaire's ruler since 1965.

Alliance rebels say armed Hutus among the refugees from the former Rwandan government army and extremist Interahamwe militia who played a leading role in the 1994 Rwandan genocide pose a grave security threat.
